data.description:
## Symptom

Two test modules fail when the full suite runs, and pass when run on their own:

- `tests/interfaces/facades/test_plan_review_attestation_facades.py`
- `tests/interfaces/facades/test_verify_completion_facades.py`

The failure surfaces as a logging teardown error rather than an assertion:

```
Logging error: I/O operation on closed file
```

## Evidence

- **Confirmed independently twice**, by two separate agents working from different worktrees.
- **Reproduces on a pristine, unmodified `origin/main` checkout** — it is not caused by any
  in-flight change.
- Run in isolation the modules pass: 35/35 observed green.
- Neither module references the code that was in flight when the failure was first seen, so
  the coupling is to suite *order*, not to subject matter.

This is order-dependent and pre-existing. It is filed as a bug rather than retried, per the
project rule that a flaky test is a bug to root-cause and never a retry.

## Likely shape (hypotheses, unproven)

Each remains to be distinguished by experiment; none is yet supported by evidence beyond the
error text:

1. An earlier test closes a stream that a module-scoped or session-scoped logging handler still
   holds, so the handler writes to a closed file during this module's teardown.
2. `caplog`/`capsys` teardown interacts with a handler installed at import time by one of the
   facade modules and never removed.
3. A `logging.shutdown()` or handler-removal side effect from an unrelated module leaks across
   test boundaries.

## Suggested first step

Find the minimal failing pair with `pytest -p no:randomly` plus a bisect over the preceding
modules (`--deselect`, or `pytest-bisect`-style halving) to identify the specific predecessor
that triggers it. Capture the handler inventory (`logging.root.handlers` and the facade
loggers' handlers) at the start and end of the predecessor to see which handler's stream is
closed and who closed it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The specific predecessor test (or fixture) whose teardown closes the stream is identified
      and named, with a deterministic two-module reproduction command.
- [ ] The root cause is fixed at the class level (handler/stream lifetime), not by reordering,
      skipping, or marking either facade module.
- [ ] Both facade modules pass in the full `make test` selection and in isolation.
- [ ] A regression guard exists that would fail if the same handler-lifetime leak is
      reintroduced.

## Out of scope

Reordering the suite, adding `-p no:randomly` to the default selection, or any change that
hides the ordering dependency rather than removing it.
data.title: Facade attestation tests fail in full-suite order with "I/O operation on closed file", pass in isolation
